steps.narration: Want to know who has already read the new policy? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll show you how to upload and send documents.
Documents keeps contracts, policies and certificates in one place. Employees read and sign them right in the app.
In the left menu, under Company, I open Documents. They're managed by an administrator or a user with the Document manager right.
The list shows the folder, recipients, confirmation status and expiration. Folders are on the left, and All documents holds absolutely everything.
You create folders in Settings. I click Add folder and create a folder for HR policies.
I type a name and a short description. In User permissions, you can let selected people read the whole folder.

actions.value: Policies and internal rules for all employees.

steps.narration: I click Create folder. The new folder shows up in the list right away, and you can file documents in it.
On the Approvals tab, you can turn on mandatory approval for documents that employees upload themselves. An administrator or document manager approves them.
In Notifications, you set how often Sloneek reminds people about unread and unsigned documents, and when it warns about an upcoming expiration.
Back in Documents, I click Add new document. You can create a document from a template or upload your own file.
You can upload for the whole company, for a single user, or in bulk for several people. I'll upload the policy as a company-wide document.
I type the name Remote work policy and pick the HR policies folder.
I upload the file, a PDF or an image. The private email toggle would also send the finished document to a private address, so I leave it off.
In Document owner, you decide who gets the document: the whole company, selected teams, or individual users.
For this example, I choose Selected users and pick James Miller from the list.
Under Expand, there are more options, such as the expiration date and a version label. For the version, I type 1.0.
steps.narration_tts: Under Expand, there are more options, such as the expiration date and a version label. For the version, I type one point oh.

steps.narration: The confirmation type can be Not required, Read confirmation, or Signature request. For a policy, a read confirmation is enough.
I tick the deadline and set it to fourteen days. Below, you can also set a deadline for new colleagues, counted from their first sign-in.
Finally, I add an accompanying message and click Confirm. Recipients get an email notification and find the document in the app.

actions.value: Please read the new remote work policy and confirm it.

steps.narration: The document is first in the list. The Status column shows how many people have confirmed it, so far zero out of one.
Clicking the name opens the detail. The preview is on the left, and on the right you can edit the name, folder, expiration or version.
The Confirmations tab shows the status for each recipient. Remind sends a reminder, and once it's read, you can download the confirmation here.
Contracts and amendments go to one person. I close the detail and choose Upload single user document.
I type the name, select James as the document owner, and upload the agreement file.
I expand the settings and choose Signature request. I set the deadline date two weeks ahead.
You can add more signers, such as a director, from your colleagues. To send the document to someone outside the company, use Add external user.
I click Confirm. The Status column now shows the signing status, so far zero out of one.
No need to write recurring contracts from scratch. In Templates, you prepare text with variables that are filled in from the employee profile.
For example, the name, position or start date. With Order of signatures, you decide who signs first.
Employees see their documents under My documents. In the Status column, they click Sign or confirm that they've read the document.
You can also see what was sent to whom in the employee profile, on the Documents tab. James has both new documents here.
Who can manage documents is set in the user profile, under Special user rights, by choosing Document manager.
Under the three dots, you can download, duplicate, archive, move to another folder, or delete a document. Archive outdated documents instead, because deleting can't be undone.
A final tip: with HR Workflows, Sloneek can automatically send new colleagues a document from a template, for example on their first day.
Now you know how to upload a document, send it to be read or signed, and track who has confirmed it. If something doesn't work, check the Help Center.
Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
